instruction: Locate the personal homepages for the last three authors in the research paper and add them as bookmarks under a folder titled 'Liked Authors'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-20)

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying the last three authors from the PDF (De-An Huang, Yuke Zhu, Anima Anandkumar), searching for their professional websites, and bookmarking them in a folder named 'Liked Authors'. Uses the same is_expected_bookmarks metric. Similar complexity to original task with focus on different set of authors.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: (1) identifies the last 3 authors from PDF, (2) searches for their personal homepages, (3) bookmarks them in a folder named 'Liked Authors'

Folder name alignment verified: Instruction specifies 'Liked Authors' (line 6), expected.rules.names contains 'Liked Authors' (line 82), and metric function hardcodes 'Liked Authors' (chrome.py:220) - all three are consistent
Getter logic is correct: get_bookmarks (chrome.py:465) retrieves Chrome bookmarks data from the Bookmarks file, which provides the full bookmark structure needed for verification

Metric logic is correct: is_expected_bookmarks with type 'liked_authors_websites_urls' (chrome.py:218-242) searches for the 'Liked Authors' folder in bookmark_bar, extracts URLs from that folder, and uses itertools.product to flexibly match against the expected author homepage URLs
URL matching is flexible and robust: The metric accepts any valid homepage URL from the provided alternatives for each author (multiple acceptable URLs per author account for homepage variations)
Complete verification coverage: The evaluator checks both (1) folder existence with correct name and (2) presence of correct author homepage URLs in that folder
